papers.titleEn: Molecular Bridging Enables Uniform and Solvent-Resilient Buried Contacts for Efficient and Stable Perovskite/TOPCon Tandem Solar Cells
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Self‐assembled monolayers (SAMs) enable high‐performance inverted perovskite solar cells and perovskite/silicon tandem solar cells, but polar solvents can partially disrupt preformed SAMs and produce nonuniform buried contacts, a challenge amplified on silicon substrates. Here, 3‐(9H‐carbazol‐9‐yl)propan‐1‐aminium iodide (CzPA) is introduced as a molecular bridge at the SAM/perovskite buried interface. The carbazole unit promotes π–π interactions with the SAM, improving monolayer retention during solvent exposure, while the terminal ammonium group interacts with iodide‐containing precursor species to regulate interfacial nucleation. Furthermore, the iodide ions can effectively passivate the iodide vacancies at the buried interface. The reconstructed interface accelerates early‐stage nucleation, promotes orientationally ordered crystal growth, and reduces residual tensile stress, thereby yielding a more p‐type heterojunction and effectively suppressing non‐radiative recombination. CzPA‐modified wide‐bandgap inverted single‐junction cells deliver a PCE of 23.79%. Applied to perovskite/tunnel oxide passivating contact (TOPCon) tandems, this strategy improves perovskite continuity in pyramid valleys, enabling 1 cm 2 devices with a PCE of 33.4%. Unencapsulated tandems retain 88% of their initial PCE after 800 h of one‐sun maximum‐power‐point tracking and 90% of their post‐burn‐in PCE after 737 h at 85°C, underscoring the robustness of the reconstructed buried interface.
papers.filename: Xuegong Yu, Adv. Funct. Mater., 2026, Molecular Bridging Enables Uniform and Solvent-Resilient Buried Contacts for Efficient and Stable Perovskite TOPCon Tandem Solar Cells

papers.titleEn: Defect-Engineering-Tailored Triple-Enzyme-Mimetic Heterojunction Nanozyme-Based Colorimetric Sensor Array for AI-Powered On-Site Intelligent Assay of Multiple Antibiotic Residues
papers.abstract: Abstract Maintaining high levels of multienzyme-like activities within a single nanoparticle-based sensing array to boost the efficient simultaneous on-site assay of multiple antibiotic residues at low regulatory threshold levels is critical for the “One Health” initiative, but remains an ongoing challenge. Herein, a defect-engineered Pt−CuO/Cu2O heterojunction nanozyme was rationally designed with enhanced peroxidase- (POD), oxidase- (OXD), and laccase-like (LAC) activities, in which each component performs its designated function with efficient coordination. The introduction of Pt sites and increased oxygen vacancy (OV) through defect engineering modulate the heterointerface electronic structure and optimize the d-band center, as corroborated by density functional theory calculations. Such electronic modulation enhances the adsorption energy of Pt−CuO/Cu2O towards the substrates such as H2O2 (−1.02 eV to −1.49 eV) and O2 (−0.76 eV to −1.12 eV), thus boosting its triple-enzyme-like catalytic performance concurrently. Leveraging the distinct modulatory effects of β-lactams (BLs), tetracyclines (TCs), and fluoroquinolones (FQs) on these three enzyme-like activities, a single-receptor, three-channel colorimetric sensing array was constructed. Coupled with a home-made, highly-integrated and portable device for RGB signal acquisition and machine learning-assisted classification-regression models, the array achieved accurate on-site intelligent analysis of the three types of antibiotics across 0.2 μM to 100.0 μM within only 15.0 min, with performance approaching and even exceeding the regulatory limits. Performing the on-site assay on spiked milk powder samples produced satisfactory accuracy and recoveries, which were validated against authoritative LC−MS. This work establishes a defect-engineering paradigm for maintaining triple-enzyme-mimetic activities at high catalytic levels in a single nanoparticle-based efficient sensing array, enabling the on-site sensitive and accurate discrimination of multiple antibiotic residues at low concentrations through a machine learning-assisted colorimetric sensing array, thus offering both theoretical guidance and a deployable solution for food safety monitoring of multiple antibiotic residues.
papers.filename: Yizhong Shen, Anal. Chem., 2026, Defect-Engineering-Tailored Triple-Enzyme-Mimetic Heterojunction Nanozyme-Based Colorimetric Sensor Array for AI-Powered On-Site Intelligent Assay

papers.titleEn: Insights into Dual-Cure UV-Induced Photopolymerization and Thermal Curing of Phthalonitrile Resins
papers.abstract: Abstract Phthalonitrile (PN) resins are well recognized for their exceptional thermal stability. However, their practical implementation is often limited by the high temperatures required to initiate thermal curing. This study reports the development of an ionic-liquid-assisted dual-cure strategy to produce processable PN-based thermosets under significantly reduced curing conditions. The thermosets were prepared using photopolymerizable formulations containing an acrylate-functionalized PN monomer in the presence of a crosslinker (poly(ethylene glycol) diacrylate) and the ionic liquid 1-butyl-3-methylimidazolium dicyanamide as a curing promoter. Solvent-free UV polymerization produced a polyacrylate scaffold in which the PN functionality remains chemically intact, enabling subsequent network formation during thermal curing. The relationships between material composition and physical properties, including thermal behavior, thermal stability, and thermomechanical performance, are reported. Combined spectroscopic, calorimetric, computational, and thermomechanical analyses suggest that the ionic liquid enables early-stage activation of the network during thermal treatment and promotes subsequent PN crosslinking into a rigid heteroaromatic thermoset structure. As a result, highly thermally robust PN-containing materials were obtained under substantially milder curing conditions than those typically associated with conventional PN systems. These findings not only contribute to a deeper understanding of PN curing mechanisms but also establish ionic-liquid-assisted dual curing as an effective route to advanced PN thermosets with improved processability and exceptional thermal performance.
papers.filename: James D. Sitter, Macromolecules, 2026, Insights into Dual-Cure UV-Induced Photopolymerization and Thermal Curing of Phthalonitrile Resins

papers.titleEn: Multifunctional Molecular Bridge for Synergistic Interfacial Regulation Toward Efficient Perovskite Solar Cells
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT The performance of self‐assembled monolayers (SAMs) in perovskite solar cells (PSCs) is frequently hindered by molecular aggregation, poor interfacial wettability, and high buried‐interface defect density. Herein, we introduce 4‐carboxyphenylboronic acid (CPBA) as a multifunctional molecular bridge to synergistically engineer the buried interface through co‐assembly with Me‐4PACz. CPBA anchors its carboxylic groups onto the NiO x substrate, refining SAM morphology and enhancing wettability, while its exposed boronic acid (‐B(OH) 2 ) groups multifunctionally passivate perovskite interfacial defects via Lewis acid‐base coordination and hydrogen bonding, and its strong molecular dipole optimizes energy‐level alignment for efficient hole extraction. Moreover, CPBA modulates perovskite crystallization kinetics, yielding high‐quality films with enlarged grains and reduced grain‐boundary defects. Consequently, CPBA‐modified PSCs achieved a power conversion efficiency of 26.02%, with an open‐circuit voltage of 1.191 V and a fill factor of 83.67%. Unencapsulated devices maintained 91% of their initial efficiency after 1800 h of storage and 88% after 1300 h of thermal aging at 65°C. This molecular‐bridging strategy provides a robust pathway toward efficient and durable perovskite photovoltaics.
papers.filename: Jun Pan, Small, 2026, Multifunctional Molecular Bridge for Synergistic Interfacial Regulation Toward Efficient Perovskite Solar Cells
